definition: AbstractConcreteDisjoint abstract concrete means ∀ x, abstract x → ¬ concrete x, for independently supplied classification predicates. It does not define either classification or assert that every candidate belongs to one of them.
note: Required classification policy for the intended P2-B/P3 wrapper, alongside its exercise-to-thin-power dictionary and owner power-to-concrete constraint. The generic predicate alone remains a proposition, not a theorem about arbitrary labels. It imposes neither exhaustiveness nor a ban on incoming abstract causation, and does not classify passive recipients as abstract. See docs/notes/causal-power-concreteness.md. #1103: the same proposition is the required disjoint field of the shared Classification (DEF-CONCRETE-ABSTRACT-CLASSIFICATION); for the adopted esse sense it is derived, not stipulated (DEF-ABSTRACT-NO-ESSE-IN-RE). #1111 API boundary: Classification.disjoint is a proof projection from a structure already containing these predicates and their disjointness; it is not a standalone predicate constructor to alias. DefinitionDictionaryConnections.connections checks that this proposition is equivalent to existence of a Classification with exactly the supplied abstract and concrete predicates. No classification criterion, exhaustiveness or disjointness for arbitrary predicates follows; both existing APIs are preserved, avoiding a lower-level dependency on the causal wrapper.
